articles.headline_en: Saxony’s Interior Ministry Deletes Controversial Post About Berlin’s Left Party
articles.summary_en: Saxony’s Interior Ministry deleted a post published on its official Instagram and X accounts after Berlin’s Left Party took legal action. The post, by Interior Minister Armin Schuster, linked the party’s Berlin election victory to concerns about antisemitism and criminal clans and called the result a “slap in the face to law-abiding citizens”; Schuster denied intending to damage a political rival.

articles.headline_en: Berlin’s Left Party Takes Action Against Saxony’s Interior Minister
articles.summary_en: The Berlin Left Party pursued legal action over an Instagram post by Saxony Interior Minister Armin Schuster concerning the party’s election victory. The party argued that the remarks violated its right to equal opportunities and sought a cease-and-desist declaration by October 2.

articles.headline_en: Saxony’s Interior Ministry Deletes Social-Media Post About Berlin’s Left Party
articles.summary_en: After legal action by Berlin’s Left Party, Saxony’s Interior Ministry removed a social-media post about the party’s election victory. The ministry had distributed the post through its official Instagram and X accounts; the Left Party also sent similar legal letters concerning social-media remarks by other politicians.

articles.headline_en: Turkey Censors the Country’s Censorship Watchdog as Crackdown on Dissent Intensifies
articles.summary_en: X made the account of EngelliWeb, a Turkish digital-rights watchdog, inaccessible to users in Turkey after receiving an order from the Cybersecurity Presidency. The report says the order relied on Article 8/A of Turkey’s Internet Act and that authorities ordered the blocking of at least 1,270 X accounts during September, with X geo-blocking about 90% of them in Turkey.

articles.headline_en: Mediapart Says It Authenticated the Antisemitic Messages Attributed to Jordan Bardella
articles.summary_en: Mediapart published screenshots of allegedly antisemitic messages attributed to Jordan Bardella and said it had authenticated them through Facebook and a bailiff. The messages were reportedly sent to another person through Messenger in 2013.

articles.headline_en: Election Panel Orders Netanyahu to Remove Campaign Videos
articles.summary_en: An election panel ordered Benjamin Netanyahu to remove campaign videos from both official social-media channels and his personal accounts. The report describes separate orders covering the different accounts.

editorial_overview: The articles show several forms of contested political speech online across Europe and its wider regional context. In Germany, a government ministry removed an official post after legal pressure from a political party, while related disputes continued over politicians’ social-media accusations. In Turkey, authorities reportedly targeted a digital-rights watchdog and continued broad account blocking under national-security and public-order provisions. Other reports concerned alleged historical private messages attributed to a French politician and an Israeli election-panel order requiring campaign material to be removed.
topic: European press review: political speech, social-media removals and censorship, September 30–October 7, 2026
